gaps.sentence: We ___ to Greece for our honeymoon, but that was twenty years ago.
gaps.hint: twenty years ago fixes a finished past
gaps.explanation: A finished time expression like 'twenty years ago' demands the past simple: went.

gaps.sentence: Hardly a week ___ without some new scandal hitting the headlines.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly a week goes by' = weeks rarely pass without something happening.

gaps.sentence: When I got home, I realised I ___ my keys at the office.
gaps.explanation: 'Had left' — the leaving happened before the realising.

gaps.sentence: I ___ that film three times, and I would happily watch it again.
gaps.hint: life experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Experience up to the present with no specific past time takes the present perfect: have seen.

gaps.sentence: While I ___ the report yesterday, my laptop battery died.
gaps.hint: the battery died interrupted the writing
gaps.explanation: The dying battery interrupted the ongoing writing, so the past continuous fits: was writing.

gaps.sentence: My back hurts because I ___ the garden all afternoon.
gaps.hint: all afternoon explains the present pain
gaps.explanation: A recent continuous activity with a visible present result takes the present perfect continuous: have been digging.

gaps.sentence: By the time I woke up, my flatmates ___ to work.
gaps.hint: by the time plus past simple
gaps.explanation: 'By the time' plus a past action refers back to an earlier past action, so the past perfect is needed: had gone.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time she ___ a car on her own.
gaps.hint: it was the first time takes past perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It was the first time' in past contexts, English uses the past perfect: had driven.
